returns: log returns in excess of T-bills
note: Arithmetic on the published forecast for two declared composites and cash; not a model, selects nothing, no out-of-sample evidence of its own

frontier.method: Arithmetic on the published forecast, not a model and not a tested strategy. Weights x are shares of capital, long-only, at most 100% of capital in all; the rest is cash. There is no borrowing. drift_i = mean_12m_i + 0.5 cov_annual_ii. volatility = sqrt(x'cov_annual x). growth = x'drift - 0.5 x'cov_annual x, the expected log excess return of the portfolio rebalanced to x; for one asset it equals mean_12m, for a mix it exceeds x'mean_12m (the approximation of the published portfolio rows) by 0.5 (sum x_i cov_ii - x'cov x). growth_lo/growth_hi = growth -/+ sum_i x_i (ci90_hi_i - ci90_lo_i)/2: the 90% intervals of the means added as if perfectly correlated; sampling error of the means only. Curve 'fully_invested': least variance per level of drift with sum(x) = 1. Curve 'with_cash': the same with sum(x) <= 1, from all cash to the asset with the highest drift. Points: min_variance and max_sharpe (most drift per unit of volatility) are long-only and fully invested; risk_parity gives every asset the same share of portfolio variance; 'match' rows are the with_cash frontier at a policy portfolio's volatility (at its top when the policy portfolio is more volatile), with gap = its growth minus the policy portfolio's and gap_lo/gap_hi = gap -/+ sum_i |x_i - w_i| (ci90_hi_i - ci90_lo_i)/2, the widest the 90% intervals of the means allow.
